target_units.text: When I say to the lawless person, ‘You will surely be put to death,’ and you do not warn him or speak to warn the lawless person to turn from his ways so that he may live, that lawless person will die in his injustice; but I will require his blood from your hand.

retained_triples.relationship: repeated distinction between rejected warning and the prophet's responsibility
retained_triples.rationale: Both passages say that a warned person who refuses to turn dies in his own wrongdoing, while the prophet who delivered the warning rescues his own life.

retained_triples.rationale: Israel says its lawless deeds lie upon it and asks how it can live while wasting away. Leviticus predicts that survivors waste away because of their sins and then confess their own and their fathers' sins.

retained_triples.source_text: and returns a pledge, repays what he seized and walks in the ordinances of life without doing wrong, he will surely live and certainly will not die.

retained_triples.relationship: repeated non-remembrance of former sins after repentance

target_units.text: None of the transgressions he committed will be remembered. By the righteousness he practiced, he will live.

retained_triples.relationship: repeated dispute over whose way is crooked

target_units.text: You said, ‘The Lord’s way does not run straight.’ Hear now, the whole house of Israel: Surely My way does not fail to run straight? Is it not your way that fails to run straight?

retained_triples.relationship: repeated consequence of turning from righteousness

target_units.text: When the righteous person turns from his righteousness, commits a transgression and dies, in the transgression he committed—in it he will die.

retained_triples.relationship: repeated preservation of life through turning from lawlessness
retained_triples.rationale: Both passages describe the lawless person turning to judgment and righteousness and living. The earlier passage explicitly states that this person has preserved his life.

target_units.text: When a lawless person turns from the lawlessness he practiced and practices judgment and righteousness, this one has preserved his life

retained_triples.relationship: repeated complaint followed by individual judgment
retained_triples.rationale: Both passages repeat Israel's objection to God's way and announce judgment on each person according to that person's way. The earlier passage additionally calls for turning from impiety.
retained_triples.source_text: This is what you said: “The Lord’s way is not straight.” I will judge you, each in his ways, house of Israel.’”

target_units.text: The house of Israel says, ‘The Lord’s way does not go right.’ Surely My way does not fail to go right, house of Israel? Is it not your way that fails to go right?

retained_triples.relationship: narrative arrival corresponding to the promised survivor's report
retained_triples.rationale: The source records a survivor from Jerusalem announcing that the city has been captured. The earlier oracle anticipates a survivor coming to announce the loss and the prophet's mouth opening toward him.

retained_triples.relationship: particular covenant judgments of beasts, sword and death

then I too will walk with you in contrary anger, and I too will strike you seven times in return for your sins.

retained_triples.rationale: The source attributes the land's devastation to the people's abominations. Leviticus places ruined images, desolate holy places, cities and land within the consequences of covenant disobedience.

and I will make your cities desolate, and lay waste your holy places; and I will in no wise smell the savour of your sacrifices;
and I Myself will desolate your land, and your enemies who dwell in it shall marvel at it.

retained_triples.rationale: Both passages gather Israel from the lands of dispersion and restore the people to their own land and pasture. Jeremiah additionally promises new shepherds and a righteous Davidic ruler.

retained_triples.relationship: contrast between promised care and failed shepherding
retained_triples.rationale: God promises to seek, restore, bind and strengthen the flock, guarding the strong. Zechariah's shepherd fails to attend, seek, heal or guide and instead consumes the flock. Ezekiel's guarding of the strong is preserved.
retained_triples.source_text: I will seek the lost, bring back the wandering, bind up the broken, strengthen the failing and guard the strong. I will feed them with judgment.

target_units.text: Look, I am raising up a shepherd over the land: he will certainly not attend to what is failing, seek what is scattered, heal what is broken or guide what is whole. He will devour the flesh of the choice ones and wrench their ankle bones.

retained_triples.relationship: related recovery of the lost sheep
retained_triples.rationale: The source's first promise is to seek the lost and bring back the wandering. The parable depicts a shepherd finding a lost sheep and relates the rejoicing to a sinner's repentance; its scope is narrower than Ezekiel's whole list of care.
retained_triples.source_text: I will seek the lost, bring back the wandering, bind up the broken, strengthen the failing and guard the strong. I will feed them with judgment.

target_units.text: “What man among you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he finds it?
And when he finds it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
When he comes home, he calls his friends and neighbors together and says to them, ‘Rejoice with me, because I found my sheep that was lost!’
I tell you, in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need of repentance.

retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel distinguishes among sheep, rams and male goats. Matthew depicts the gathered nations being separated as a shepherd separates sheep from goats; the target develops a judgment scene with right and left positions not stated in Ezekiel.

retained_triples.relationship: same-chapter accusation recast as its consequence for the flock
retained_triples.rationale: The source accuses the well-fed sheep of trampling pasture and muddying water. The next unit repeats those acts from the dependent sheep's perspective: they ate the trampled pasture and drank the disturbed water.
retained_triples.source_text: Was it not enough for you that you grazed the good pasture, yet trampled the rest of your pasture with your feet, drank the settled water and troubled the rest with your feet?

target_units.text: My sheep grazed what your feet had trampled and drank the water troubled by your feet.

retained_triples.relationship: same-chapter contrast between privileged consumption and the flock's remainder
retained_triples.rationale: The source describes the sheep eating trampled pasture and drinking disturbed water. The preceding accusation identifies the privileged animals that enjoyed the good pasture and settled water before spoiling what remained.
retained_triples.source_text: My sheep grazed what your feet had trampled and drank the water troubled by your feet.

target_units.text: Was it not enough for you that you grazed the good pasture, yet trampled the rest of your pasture with your feet, drank the settled water and troubled the rest with your feet?

retained_triples.relationship: related judgment portrayed through distinguishing among flock members
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel distinguishes strong sheep from weak sheep amid the indictment of abusive flock members. Matthew also represents judgment of people through a shepherd separating a flock, but distinguishes sheep from goats rather than strong from weak sheep.
retained_triples.source_text: Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I will distinguish between the strong sheep and the weak sheep.

target_units.text: All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them from one another as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
He will stand the sheep at His right and the young goats at His left.

retained_triples.relationship: same-chapter extension of blame from shepherds to abusive flock members
retained_triples.rationale: The source accuses animals of using shoulders and horns to force out failing sheep. Earlier the shepherds were faulted for not strengthening the weak and wearing down the strong; both expose failures to care for vulnerable members, with different actors.
retained_triples.source_text: You shove with your sides and shoulders; you butted with your horns and forced out every failing one.

target_units.text: You have not strengthened the weak, restored the sick to health, bound up the broken, brought back the wandering or sought the lost. You have worn down the strong with toil.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel restoration of a flock to safety
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises to save the sheep from plunder and judge within the flock. Jeremiah promises restored pasture and shepherds under whom the sheep will no longer fear. Jeremiah does not include the source's judgment between rams.
retained_triples.source_text: I will save My sheep, and they certainly will no longer be plunder. I will judge between ram and ram.

target_units.text: And I will receive the remnant of My people from all the land where I drove them out, and establish them in their pasture; they will increase and multiply.
And I will raise shepherds for them who will tend them, and they will no longer fear or be frightened, says the Lord.

retained_triples.relationship: repeated promise of David and one shepherd
retained_triples.rationale: Both passages designate God's servant David as ruler or shepherd and place the people under one shepherd. The later passage also connects this leadership with keeping God's ordinances.
retained_triples.source_text: I will raise up one shepherd over them, My servant David, and he will shepherd them and be their shepherd.

target_units.text: My servant David will be ruler among them, and one shepherd will be over all, because they will walk in My ordinances, keep My judgments and do them.

retained_triples.relationship: related promise of unity under one shepherd
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises one shepherd, called God's servant David. Jesus says the sheep He brings will become one flock with one shepherd. This links the shared shepherd-and-unity language without treating the passages as identical wording.
retained_triples.source_text: I will raise up one shepherd over them, My servant David, and he will shepherd them and be their shepherd.

target_units.text: And I have other sheep that are not from this fold. I must bring them also, and they will hear My voice, and they will become one flock, one shepherd.

retained_triples.relationship: repeated combination of Davidic rule and covenant belonging
retained_triples.rationale: Both passages place David among the people as ruler and declare that the Lord is their God. The later oracle expands this with an everlasting covenant and God's dwelling among them.
retained_triples.source_text: I, the Lord, will be their God, and David a ruler among them. I, the Lord, have spoken.

target_units.text: My servant David will be ruler among them, and one shepherd will be over all, because they will walk in My ordinances, keep My judgments and do them.
They will dwell upon their land, which I gave My servant Jacob, where their fathers dwelt. They will dwell upon it, and David My servant will be their ruler for ever.
I will make a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting covenant with them. I will set My holy things among them for ever.
My dwelling will be among them. I will be their God, and they will be My people.

retained_triples.relationship: shared promise of peace and removal of harmful beasts

retained_triples.source_text: I will make a covenant of peace with David and remove harmful beasts from the land. They will dwell in the wilderness and sleep in the woods.

target_units.text: And war shall not pass through your land. I will give peace in your land. You shall lie down, with no one to frighten you, and I will destroy harmful animals from your land.

retained_triples.relationship: shared promise of beneficial rain

retained_triples.source_text: I will place them around My mountain and give you rain, rain of blessing.

target_units.text: then I will give you rain in its season. The land shall yield its produce, and the trees of the fields shall yield their fruit.

retained_triples.source_text: The trees in the plain will give their fruit, and the land will give its strength. They will dwell upon their land in hope of peace and know that I am the Lord when I shatter their yoke. I will rescue them from the hand of those who enslaved them.

retained_triples.source_text: I will raise up a plant of peace for them. They will no longer perish by famine upon the land or bear the nations’ reproach.

target_units.text: The Lord answered His people: “Look, I am sending out to you grain, wine and oil, and you will be filled with them. I will no longer give you over to reproach among the nations,

and I will drive away from you the one from the north and thrust it into a waterless land. I will make its front disappear into the first sea and its rear into the last sea; its decay will rise, and its stench will rise, because it magnified its deeds.”
Take courage, land! Rejoice and be glad, because the Lord has done great things.
Take courage, animals of the plain, because the wilderness plains have sprouted, because a tree bore its fruit; vine and fig tree have given their strength.
Children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the Lord your God, because He gave you food for righteousness, and He will rain upon you early and late rainfall as before.
Threshing floors will be filled with grain, and winepresses will overflow with wine and oil.
“I will repay you for the years the locust devoured, the bruchus locust, the blight and the caterpillar—My great force that I sent among you.

retained_triples.relationship: shared covenant declaration of God and His people

retained_triples.source_text: They will know that I am the Lord their God, and they, Israel’s house, are My people, says the Lord.

target_units.text: and I will walk among you and be your God, and you shall be My people.

retained_triples.source_text: You are My sheep and the sheep of My flock, and I am the Lord your God, says the Lord, the Lord.’”

target_units.text: Know that the Lord—He is God. He made us, and not we; His people and the sheep of His pasture.

retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel charges Seir with lasting enmity and treacherous attack during Israel's final time of injustice. Obadiah records violence against Jacob and participation in Jerusalem's calamity, then forbids destroying those escaping and shutting in fugitives.
retained_triples.source_text: Because you became an everlasting enemy and ambushed Israel’s house treacherously, by enemies’ hand, with a sword at the final time of injustice,

From the day you stood opposed, on the day foreigners took his strength captive and strangers entered his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.
Do not look on your brother’s day, on the day of strangers; do not rejoice over the sons of Judah on the day of their destruction; do not speak boastfully on the day of affliction.

Do not enter the gates of peoples on the day of their suffering. You, too, must not look on their assembly on the day of their destruction, and do not join in attacking their strength on the day of their destruction.
Do not stand at their escape routes to destroy those of them who are being saved, and do not shut in those fleeing from them on the day of affliction.

retained_triples.relationship: related requital for shedding blood

target_units.text: “And surely I will require your blood, the blood of your lives. From every beast I will require it, and from the hand of a fellow man I will require the life of man.
Whoever sheds the blood of man, his own blood shall be shed in return; for in the image of God I made man.

retained_triples.rationale: God announces Mount Seir's desolation and the destruction of human beings and livestock. retained_triples.source_text: I will make Mount Seir a wilderness and lay it waste, and destroy human beings and livestock from it,

My sword became drunk in heaven. Behold, it will descend upon Idumea and upon the people of destruction, with judgment.
The Lord’s sword was filled with blood, thickened with lambs’ fat and the fat of male goats and rams, for the Lord has a sacrifice in Bosor and a great slaughter in Idumea.
The stout ones will fall with them, and rams and bulls; the earth will become drunk with blood and be filled with their fat.

night and day. It will not be quenched for an everlasting time, and her smoke will rise upward. For generations and a long time she will be deserted.
Birds, hedgehogs, ibises and ravens will dwell in her; a measuring cord for deserted land will be cast upon her, and donkey-centaurs will dwell in her.
Her rulers will be no more, for her kings, her rulers and her magnates will come to destruction.
Thorny trees will sprout in their cities and her fortifications; she will become a dwelling for sirens and a courtyard for ostriches.

I formed it; now I brought it. It became a carrying away into exiles of fighting men—fortified cities.
Their inhabitants grew weak in hand, cowered, and were ashamed. They became field grass or green herbage, rooftop grass, and a trampling before one standing.
I know your sitting, your going out, your coming in, and your anger against Me.
Because you were angry with Me and your arrogance rose to My ears, I shall put My hooks in your nostrils and a bridle in your lips, and turn you back by the road on which you came.
