retained_triples.source_text: Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Surely in the fire of My wrath I have spoken against the remaining nations and all Idumea, because they gave My land to themselves as a possession with rejoicing, dishonoring lives so as to destroy through plunder.

target_units.text: From the day you stood opposed, on the day foreigners took his strength captive and strangers entered his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.
Do not look on your brother’s day, on the day of strangers; do not rejoice over the sons of Judah on the day of their destruction; do not speak boastfully on the day of affliction.

Do not enter the gates of peoples on the day of their suffering. You, too, must not look on their assembly on the day of their destruction, and do not join in attacking their strength on the day of their destruction.
Do not stand at their escape routes to destroy those of them who are being saved, and do not shut in those fleeing from them on the day of affliction.
For the day of the Lord is near against all the nations. Just as you acted, so it will be for you; your recompense will be repaid upon your own head.

retained_triples.relationship: related reproach of Israel and appeal to divine jealousy
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel's Lord speaks in jealousy and wrath because the land bore the nations' reproaches. The psalm places the neighbors' ridicule beside its question about God's anger and jealousy; it is a plea, whereas Ezekiel announces God's response.
retained_triples.source_text: Therefore prophesy over Israel’s land and say to the mountains, hills, ravines and valleys, Thus says the Lord: Behold, I have spoken in My jealousy and My wrath because you bore the nations’ reproaches.

target_units.text: We became a reproach to our neighbors, sneering and ridicule to those around us.
How long, Lord? Wilt Thou be angry to the end? Will Thy jealousy blaze like fire?

retained_triples.relationship: parallel requital of the neighbors' insult
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel says the surrounding nations will receive their own dishonor. The psalm asks God to repay neighboring peoples for the insult they directed against Him; its sevenfold measure is not stated in Ezekiel.
retained_triples.source_text: Therefore I will raise My hand against the nations around you; these will receive their own dishonor.

target_units.text: Repay our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom their insult with which they insulted Thee, Lord.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel restored Israel consuming its land's fruit
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises that the approaching people will consume the mountains' grapes and fruit. Amos likewise joins the reversal of Israel's captivity with planting vineyards and gardens and enjoying their wine and fruit.
retained_triples.source_text: But your grapes and fruit, mountains of Israel, My people will consume, for they are drawing near.

target_units.text: I will reverse the captivity of My people Israel. They will build ruined cities and inhabit them, plant vineyards and drink their wine, plant gardens and eat their fruit.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel renewal of cultivation in restored land
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises that God's favorable attention will result in the land being cultivated and sown. Amos describes restored Israelites planting vineyards and gardens as they rebuild and inhabit the ruined land.
retained_triples.source_text: For behold, I am toward you; I will look upon you, and you will be cultivated and sown.

target_units.text: I will reverse the captivity of My people Israel. They will build ruined cities and inhabit them, plant vineyards and drink their wine, plant gardens and eat their fruit.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel rebuilding of devastated settlements
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises inhabited cities and rebuilding of devastated land. Isaiah likewise promises renewal of deserted cities and places desolated for generations; it does not specify Ezekiel's multiplication of all Israel's house.
retained_triples.source_text: I will multiply people upon you, all Israel’s house completely. The cities will be inhabited and the devastated land rebuilt.

target_units.text: They will rebuild age-old deserts and raise places formerly desolated. They will renew deserted cities laid waste for generations.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel restoration of human and animal populations
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises to multiply humans and livestock and restore former settlement. Jeremiah similarly promises to sow Israel and Judah with human and livestock seed, followed by God's watching to build and plant.
retained_triples.source_text: I will multiply humans and livestock upon you, settle you as at your beginning and do you good as in your former times. You will know that I am the Lord.

target_units.text: Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will sow Israel and Judah with human seed and livestock seed.
And just as I watched over them to tear down and harm, so I will watch over them to build and plant, says the Lord.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel secure possession of restored land
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises Israel possession of the land and says the land will no longer be bereaved of the people. Amos promises to plant the people on their given land without their being uprooted again; the images express security differently.
retained_triples.source_text: I will cause people, My people Israel, to be born upon you. They will inherit you, and you will be their possession. You certainly will no longer be bereaved of them.

target_units.text: I will plant them upon their land, and they will certainly never again be uprooted from the land I have given them,” says the Lord God Almighty.

retained_triples.relationship: repeated description of the land as devouring inhabitants
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel quotes the accusation that the land devours human beings. The scouts' dismaying report in Numbers uses the same description of a land that devours its inhabitants; the speakers and occasions differ.
retained_triples.source_text: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Because they said to you, “You devour human beings and became bereaved by your nation,”

target_units.text: And they brought dismay concerning the land which they had searched out unto the sons of Israel, saying: The land through which we passed to search it out is a land that devours its inhabitants; all the people whom we saw therein are men of exceeding height;

retained_triples.relationship: reversal of the land-devouring accusation
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises that the land will no longer eat human beings or bereave its nation. Numbers preserves the scouts' earlier accusation that the land devours its inhabitants; Ezekiel's promise negates that characterization.
retained_triples.source_text: therefore you will no longer eat human beings or bereave your nation, says the Lord, the Lord.

target_units.text: And they brought dismay concerning the land which they had searched out unto the sons of Israel, saying: The land through which we passed to search it out is a land that devours its inhabitants; all the people whom we saw therein are men of exceeding height;

retained_triples.relationship: parallel removal of the nations' reproach
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises that the land will no longer bear the peoples' reproaches. Joel likewise promises that God will no longer give His people over as a reproach among the nations, alongside renewed food supplies.
retained_triples.source_text: The nations’ dishonor will no longer be heard against you, and you certainly will not bear the peoples’ reproaches, says the Lord, the Lord.’”

target_units.text: The Lord answered His people: “Look, I am sending out to you grain, wine and oil, and you will be filled with them. I will no longer give you over to reproach among the nations,

retained_triples.relationship: ritual-uncleanness imagery applied to Israel's conduct
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel compares Israel's defiling conduct and idols with the uncleanness of a woman sitting apart. Leviticus supplies concrete regulations for menstrual uncleanness of that kind; it does not itself equate menstruation with Israel's wrongdoing.
retained_triples.source_text: “Son of man, Israel’s house lived upon their land and defiled it by their way, their idols and their uncleannesses. Their way before Me became like the uncleanness of a woman sitting apart.

target_units.text: And if a woman has a flow of blood, her flow shall be in her body; she shall remain in her menstrual discharge for seven days. Whosoever touches her shall be unclean until evening,
and everything on which she lies during her menstrual discharge shall be unclean, and everything on which she sits shall be unclean.
And whosoever touches her bed shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be unclean until evening.
And whosoever touches any article on which she sits shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
If, while she is on her bed or on the article on which she sits, he touches her, he shall be unclean until evening.
If anyone lies with her and her uncleanness comes upon him, he shall be unclean for seven days, and every bed on which he lies shall be unclean.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel covenant judgment of international scattering
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel describes God scattering Israel among nations as judgment for its conduct. Leviticus threatens scattering among the nations together with ruined land and cities as a consequence of covenant disobedience.
retained_triples.source_text: and scattered them among the nations and winnowed them into the countries. I judged them according to their way and their sin.

target_units.text: And I will scatter you among the nations, and the advancing sword shall consume you. Your land shall become desolate, and your cities shall be desolate.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel dishonor of God's name among the nations through His people
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel describes the holy name being profaned when nations see the Lord's people outside His land. Romans likewise says God's name is blasphemed among nations because of the addressed people's conduct, specifically their transgression of law.
retained_triples.source_text: They entered the nations where they entered, and profaned My holy name when it was said of them, ‘These are the Lord’s people, and they have left His land.’

target_units.text: You who boast in law, do you dishonor God through transgression of the law?
For “the name of God is blasphemed among the nations because of you,” just as it is written.

retained_triples.relationship: repeated divine action for the sake of the profaned name
retained_triples.rationale: God spares Israel because of His holy name, profaned among nations. The earlier oracle similarly says God acted so His name would not be profaned at all before nations during Israel's departure from Egypt.
retained_triples.source_text: I spared them because of My holy name, which Israel’s house profaned among the nations where they entered.

target_units.text: I acted so that My name would not be profaned at all before the nations among whom they are, among whom I was known to them before their eyes by bringing them out of Egypt’s land.

retained_triples.relationship: repeated distinction between Israel's conduct and God's concern for His name
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel says the coming action is for God's holy name rather than for Israel. The earlier wilderness account also attributes God's restraining action to protecting His name before the nations, despite the people's rebellion.
retained_triples.source_text: Therefore say to Israel’s house, ‘Thus says the Lord: I am not acting for you, house of Israel, but because of My holy name, which you profaned among the nations where you entered.

target_units.text: I acted so that My name would not be profaned at all before the nations from whom I brought them out before their eyes.

retained_triples.relationship: close parallel public sanctification before the nations
retained_triples.rationale: Both promises say God will be sanctified in the people before the nations' eyes. The earlier promise places this beside gathering them from dispersion, while the source emphasizes His profaned great name.
retained_triples.source_text: I will sanctify My great name, profaned among the nations, which you profaned among them. The nations will know that I am the Lord when I am sanctified in you before their eyes.

target_units.text: As a fragrant aroma I will accept you when I bring you out from the peoples and receive you from the countries where you were scattered. I will be sanctified among you before the eyes of the peoples.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel gathering of dispersed Israel into its ancestral land
retained_triples.rationale: Both passages promise God's gathering of Israel from nations and bringing the people into their land. Deuteronomy describes that land as the fathers' inheritance and joins gathering with mercy and increase.
retained_triples.source_text: I will take you out of the nations, gather you out of all the lands and bring you into your own land.

target_units.text: then the Lord shall heal your sins, and have mercy upon you, and shall gather you again from all the nations whither the Lord has scattered you.
If your dispersion is from one end of heaven unto the other end of heaven, from thence shall the Lord your God gather you, and from thence shall the Lord your God take you.
And the Lord your God shall bring you into the land which your fathers inherited, and you shall inherit it; and He shall do you good, and make you more numerous than your fathers.

retained_triples.relationship: related sprinkling of water for purification
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises sprinkling clean water to cleanse the people from uncleannesses and idols. Numbers prescribes sprinkling purification water on persons and objects defiled by contact with death; the kinds of impurity and the water's preparation differ.
retained_triples.source_text: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you will be cleansed from all your uncleannesses and all your idols. I will cleanse you.

target_units.text: And for the unclean person they shall take some ashes from what was burned for purification, and they shall pour living water over them into a vessel.

And a clean man shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it around the house, the vessels, and the people who were there, and on whoever touched the human bone, the slain person, the dead person, or the tomb.

And the clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. He shall be purified on the seventh day, wash his clothes, and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.

retained_triples.relationship: related combination of sprinkling, inward cleansing and pure water
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel's clean-water sprinkling removes uncleannesses and idols. Hebrews exhorts people to approach with hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and bodies washed with pure water, combining cleansing imagery in its exhortation about access to God.
retained_triples.source_text: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you will be cleansed from all your uncleannesses and all your idols. I will cleanse you.

target_units.text: let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

retained_triples.relationship: close parallel replacement of the stone heart
retained_triples.rationale: Both promises give a new spirit and replace the heart of stone with a heart of flesh. The earlier oracle says another heart, while the source says a new heart.
retained_triples.source_text: And I will give you a new heart, and I will give a new spirit within you; and I will take the heart of stone out of your flesh, and give you a heart of flesh.

target_units.text: I will give them another heart and put a new spirit within them. I will tear the stone heart from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,

retained_triples.relationship: related contrast of stone and hearts of flesh with the Spirit
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel replaces a stone heart with a heart of flesh and gives a new spirit. Paul describes Christ's letter inscribed by the living God's Spirit on hearts of flesh rather than stone tablets; the writing metaphor differs from Ezekiel's replacement of a heart.
retained_triples.source_text: And I will give you a new heart, and I will give a new spirit within you; and I will take the heart of stone out of your flesh, and give you a heart of flesh.

target_units.text: You are clearly a letter of Christ, produced through our ministry, inscribed not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on stone tablets but on tablets that are hearts of flesh.

retained_triples.relationship: close parallel inner renewal enabling obedience
retained_triples.rationale: Both passages connect the gift of spirit within the people with walking in God's ordinances and doing His judgments or commands. Ezekiel 11 additionally states the reciprocal God-and-people relationship.
retained_triples.source_text: I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My ordinances, keep My judgments and do them.

target_units.text: I will give them another heart and put a new spirit within them. I will tear the stone heart from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,
so that they may walk in My commands, keep My ordinances and carry them out. They will be My people, and I will be their God.

retained_triples.relationship: related Spirit-directed obedience to God's requirements
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises God's Spirit within the people so they keep His judgments. Romans describes God's action through His Son so the law's righteous requirement is fulfilled in those walking according to Spirit; it does not explicitly identify itself as this oracle's fulfillment.
retained_triples.source_text: I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My ordinances, keep My judgments and do them.

target_units.text: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God did: sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and concerning sin, He condemned sin in the flesh,
so that the law’s righteous requirement might be fulfilled in us who walk not according to flesh, but according to Spirit.

retained_triples.relationship: shared restored covenant relationship
retained_triples.rationale: Both promises declare that the people will be God's people and He their God. Ezekiel locates them on the land given their fathers; Jeremiah joins the relationship with God's law written within their understanding and hearts.
retained_triples.source_text: You will dwell upon the land I gave your fathers. You will be My people, and I will be your God.

target_units.text: Because this is the covenant I will make with Israel’s house after those days, says the Lord: I will surely put My laws into their understanding and write them upon their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be My people.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel provision of grain after divine restoration
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises multiplied grain and relief from famine along with cleansing. Joel promises grain, wine and oil to satisfy the people and remove national reproach; the selected verse does not repeat Ezekiel's cleansing language.
retained_triples.source_text: I will save you from all your uncleannesses, summon the grain and multiply it, and will not bring famine upon you.

target_units.text: The Lord answered His people: “Look, I am sending out to you grain, wine and oil, and you will be filled with them. I will no longer give you over to reproach among the nations,

retained_triples.relationship: parallel fruitful fields and trees ending food-related shame
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel multiplies tree fruit and field produce to remove the reproach of famine. Joel likewise promises fruitful trees, filled threshing floors and abundant eating, followed by the promise that God's people will not be put to shame.
retained_triples.source_text: I will multiply the tree’s fruit and the field’s produce, so that you do not bear the reproach of famine among the nations.

target_units.text: Take courage, animals of the plain, because the wilderness plains have sprouted, because a tree bore its fruit; vine and fig tree have given their strength.
Children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the Lord your God, because He gave you food for righteousness, and He will rain upon you early and late rainfall as before.
Threshing floors will be filled with grain, and winepresses will overflow with wine and oil.
“I will repay you for the years the locust devoured, the bruchus locust, the blight and the caterpillar—My great force that I sent among you.
You will eat abundantly and be filled, and praise the name of the Lord your God for the wonders He has done with you. My people will certainly never be put to shame,

retained_triples.relationship: close parallel remembrance of former evil with shame
retained_triples.rationale: Both promises describe remembering the ways by which Israel acted wickedly. The source expresses disgust at lawless deeds and abominations; the earlier oracle describes beating their faces because of their wickedness, without identical wording.
retained_triples.source_text: You will remember your evil ways and practices that were not good, and feel disgust before them at your lawless deeds and abominations.

target_units.text: There you will remember your ways and your practices by which you were being defiled; you will beat your faces over all your evils.

retained_triples.relationship: related denial that land possession rewards Israel's merit
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel says God is not acting because of Israel and calls the people to shame over their ways. Deuteronomy likewise denies that possession of the good land comes from Israel's righteous deeds or holy heart, calling the people stiff-necked.
retained_triples.source_text: I am not acting because of you, says the Lord, the Lord; this will be known to you. Be ashamed and abashed because of your ways, house of Israel.

target_units.text: Do not say in your heart, when the Lord your God consumes these nations from before you: Because of my righteous deeds the Lord has brought me in to inherit this good land. Rather, because of the ungodliness of these nations the Lord shall destroy them from before you.

You do not enter to inherit their land for your righteousness, nor for the holiness of your heart; but because of the ungodliness of these nations the Lord shall destroy them from before you, and that He may establish His covenant which He sware unto your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
And you shall know this day that the Lord your God does not give you this good land to inherit for your righteous deeds; for you are a stiff-necked people.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel restoration and cleansing of national wrongdoing
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel joins cleansing from lawless deeds with inhabited cities and rebuilding. Jeremiah similarly joins restoration and rebuilding of Judah and Israel with cleansing of the injustices committed against God.
retained_triples.source_text: Thus says the Lord: On the day I cleanse you from all your lawless deeds, I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the wilderness places will be rebuilt.

target_units.text: I will bring back Judah’s exiles and Israel’s exiles and build them as before.
I will cleanse them from all the injustices by which they sinned against Me. I will certainly not remember the sins they committed against Me when they departed from Me.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel cultivation replacing ruined land
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel says devastated land will again be worked. Amos describes restored Israelites rebuilding ruined cities and planting vineyards and gardens, giving concrete forms of renewed cultivation.
retained_triples.source_text: The devastated land will be worked, instead of lying devastated before every passerby’s eyes.

target_units.text: I will reverse the captivity of My people Israel. They will build ruined cities and inhabit them, plant vineyards and drink their wine, plant gardens and eat their fruit.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel transformation of devastated land into a garden
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel's devastated land becomes like a garden of delight. Isaiah likewise promises comfort to Zion's deserted places by making them like the Lord's paradise; neither comparison requires altering the source's garden wording.
retained_triples.source_text: They will say, “That devastated land has become like a garden of delight, and the deserted, devastated, razed cities stand fortified.”

target_units.text: I will now comfort you, Zion; I have comforted all her deserted places and will make her deserted places like the Lord’s paradise. They will find joy and exultation in her, thanksgiving and a voice of praise.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel reversal from destruction to building and planting
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel identifies God as the One rebuilding razed places and planting devastated places. Jeremiah likewise contrasts His former tearing down and harming with His renewed watching to build and plant.
retained_triples.source_text: The nations remaining around you will know that I, the Lord, have rebuilt the razed places and planted the devastated places. I, the Lord, have spoken and will act.

target_units.text: And just as I watched over them to tear down and harm, so I will watch over them to build and plant, says the Lord.

retained_triples.relationship: related explicit identification of human people with God's flock
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises to multiply human beings like sheep. The earlier shepherd oracle explicitly addresses the people as God's sheep and flock, supplying the same human-flock identification without the source's multiplication promise.
retained_triples.source_text: Thus says the Lord: I will also be sought by Israel’s house to do this for them: I will multiply them, human beings like sheep.

target_units.text: You are My sheep and the sheep of My flock, and I am the Lord your God, says the Lord, the Lord.’”

retained_triples.relationship: concrete festival-flock counterpart for the population comparison
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel compares cities full of people with Jerusalem's festival sheep. Chronicles describes many thousands of sheep, lambs and kids provided for Josiah's Passover; it illustrates large festival flocks without equating its numbers with Ezekiel's promised population.
retained_triples.source_text: Like holy sheep, like Jerusalem’s sheep at her festivals, so the deserted cities will be filled with sheep who are human beings. They will know that I am the Lord.’”

target_units.text: Josiah set apart for the sons of the people sheep, lambs, and kids from the offspring of goats, all for the Passover for everyone present, thirty thousand in number, and three thousand calves. These came from the king’s property.

His rulers set apart contributions for the people, priests, and Levites. Hilkiah, Zacharias, and Jiiel, rulers of God’s house, gave to the priests; they gave for the Passover two thousand six hundred sheep, lambs, and kids, and three hundred calves.
Chonenias, Banaias, Samaias, his brother Nathanael, and Asabias, Jiiel, and Jozabad, rulers of the Levites, set apart for the Levites five thousand sheep for the Passover and five hundred calves.

retained_triples.relationship: repeated visionary setting involving the Lord's hand, a plain and spirit
retained_triples.rationale: The source places Ezekiel under the Lord's hand and brings him in spirit to a plain. The earlier commission likewise has the Lord's hand upon him, sends him to the plain and describes a spirit coming upon him; the visions there differ.
retained_triples.source_text: The Lord’s hand came upon me. The Lord brought me out in spirit and set me in the middle of the plain, which was full of human bones.

target_units.text: The Lord’s hand came upon me, and He said to me, “Rise and go out to the plain, and you will be spoken to there.”
I rose and went out to the plain, and behold, the Lord’s glory stood there, like the vision and like the glory I had seen by the River Chebar; and I fall upon my face.
A spirit came upon me and set me on my feet. He spoke to me and said to me, “Go, be shut inside your house.

retained_triples.relationship: same-chapter explicit interpretation of the dry bones
retained_triples.rationale: The vision emphasizes the multitude and dryness of the bones. Its later interpretation identifies them as all Israel's house, whose saying about dry bones expresses lost hope and exhaustion.
retained_triples.source_text: He led me all around them, and behold, there were very many upon the plain’s surface, very dry.

target_units.text: The Lord spoke to me, saying, ‘Son of man, these bones are all Israel’s house, and they say, Our bones have become dry, our hope has perished; we are utterly spent.

retained_triples.relationship: question about renewed life alongside an assurance of the dead rising
retained_triples.rationale: God asks whether the bones will live, and Ezekiel leaves the answer to God's knowledge. Isaiah explicitly announces that the dead will rise and those in tombs awaken; Ezekiel's surrounding vision applies its bones to Israel's house.
retained_triples.source_text: He said to me, ‘Son of man, will these bones live?’ I said, ‘Lord, Thou knowest these things.’

target_units.text: The dead will rise, those in the tombs will be awakened, and those in the earth will rejoice, for the dew from Thee is healing to them; but the earth of the ungodly will fall.”

retained_triples.relationship: related portrayal of the dead hearing a life-giving divine word
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel must tell dry bones to hear the Lord's word. Jesus says the dead will hear the Son of God's voice and live; Ezekiel's vision explains the bones as Israel's house rather than giving John's identical setting.
retained_triples.source_text: He said to me, ‘Prophesy over these bones and say to them, Dry bones, hear the Lord’s word:

target_units.text: Amen, amen, I tell you: an hour is coming, and now is, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.

retained_triples.relationship: shared gift of the breath of life
retained_triples.rationale: God promises breath of life to the bones. Genesis describes God breathing the breath of life into the formed human so that he becomes a living soul; Ezekiel depicts restoration rather than the first human's formation.
retained_triples.source_text: Thus says the Lord to these bones: Behold, I am bringing the breath of life into you,

target_units.text: And God formed man from the dust of the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

retained_triples.relationship: shared description of bodily formation and divinely given life
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel names sinews, flesh and skin before the gift of Spirit and life. Job similarly recalls God clothing him in skin and flesh, joining bones and sinews, and granting life and care; the occasions differ.
retained_triples.source_text: and I will put sinews upon you, bring flesh upon you, stretch skin over you and put My Spirit into you. You will live and know that I am the Lord.’

target_units.text: Thou didst clothe me with skin and flesh and thread me together with bones and sinews.
Thou didst place life and mercy beside me, and Thy care guarded my spirit.

retained_triples.relationship: same-chapter narrated commencement of the promised reconstruction
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel's obedient prophecy is followed by bones joining at their joints. This begins the earlier promised reconstitution of the bones with sinews, flesh and skin, while the complete gift of life remains later in the vision.
retained_triples.source_text: I prophesied as He commanded me. As I prophesied, behold, there was a shaking, and the bones came together, each to its joint.

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord to these bones: Behold, I am bringing the breath of life into you,
and I will put sinews upon you, bring flesh upon you, stretch skin over you and put My Spirit into you. You will live and know that I am the Lord.’

retained_triples.relationship: shared bodily materials with a significant difference about life
retained_triples.rationale: The vision shows sinews, flesh and skin on the bones but still no breath. Job recalls the same bodily materials together with God's gift of life and care, highlighting the distinction between bodily formation and living animation in Ezekiel's sequence.
retained_triples.source_text: I saw, and behold, sinews and flesh grew upon them, and skin came up over them, but there was no breath in them.

target_units.text: Thou didst clothe me with skin and flesh and thread me together with bones and sinews.
Thou didst place life and mercy beside me, and Thy care guarded my spirit.

retained_triples.relationship: related breathing of life into a formed body
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel calls the breath from the four winds to breathe into the dead so they live. Genesis describes God breathing life into the human formed from dust; Genesis does not supply the four winds or the multitude of bodies.
retained_triples.source_text: He said to me, ‘Prophesy, son of man! Prophesy to the breath and say to the breath, Thus says the Lord: Come from the four winds and breathe into these dead, and let them live!’

target_units.text: And God formed man from the dust of the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

retained_triples.relationship: related breathing and reception of Spirit
retained_triples.rationale: The source commands breath to enter the dead and make them live. John describes Jesus breathing and telling the disciples to receive the Holy Spirit; this is a comparison of breathing and the divine gift of Spirit, not an identification of the disciples with Ezekiel's dead bodies.
retained_triples.source_text: He said to me, ‘Prophesy, son of man! Prophesy to the breath and say to the breath, Thus says the Lord: Come from the four winds and breathe into these dead, and let them live!’

target_units.text: Then Jesus said to them again, “Peace to you. Just as the Father has sent Me, I also send you.”
And having said this, He breathed and says to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit.

retained_triples.relationship: same-chapter realization of the promised breath and life
retained_triples.rationale: After prophecy, breath enters the bodies, they live and stand. This realizes the earlier promise that God would put breath and Spirit into the bones so that they live.
retained_triples.source_text: I prophesied as He commanded me. The breath entered them, and they lived and stood upon their feet, an exceedingly great assembly.

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord to these bones: Behold, I am bringing the breath of life into you,
and I will put sinews upon you, bring flesh upon you, stretch skin over you and put My Spirit into you. You will live and know that I am the Lord.’

retained_triples.relationship: related use of dried bones to express inward distress
retained_triples.rationale: Israel's saying that its bones are dry is explicitly joined with lost hope and exhaustion. Proverbs likewise says that a sorrowful person's bones dry up, using the bodily image for distress in an individual rather than the national vision.
retained_triples.source_text: The Lord spoke to me, saying, ‘Son of man, these bones are all Israel’s house, and they say, Our bones have become dry, our hope has perished; we are utterly spent.

target_units.text: A rejoicing heart makes one flourish, but a sorrowful man’s bones dry up.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel imagery of bringing life from tombs
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises to open the people's tombs and bring them into Israel's land. Isaiah announces that the dead will rise and those in tombs awaken; the selected Isaiah verse does not specify Ezekiel's return to Israel's land.
retained_triples.source_text: Therefore prophesy and say, Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am opening your tombs and will bring you up from your tombs and into Israel’s land,

target_units.text: The dead will rise, those in the tombs will be awakened, and those in the earth will rejoice, for the dew from Thee is healing to them; but the earth of the ungodly will fall.”

retained_triples.relationship: related image of people brought out of graves
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel links recognition of the Lord with His opening graves and bringing His people up. Jesus describes those in tombs hearing His voice and coming out to resurrection of life or judgment; Ezekiel's surrounding explanation concerns restoration of Israel's house.
retained_triples.source_text: and you will know that I am the Lord when I open your graves to bring My people up from the graves.

target_units.text: Do not marvel at this, because an hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear His voice
and come out: those who did good things to a resurrection of life, but those who practiced base things to a resurrection of judgment.

retained_triples.relationship: related promise of life through God's indwelling Spirit
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises Spirit within the people, life and placement on their land. Romans promises that the One who raised Christ will give life to believers' mortal bodies through His indwelling Spirit; it does not include Ezekiel's land promise.
retained_triples.source_text: I will put My Spirit into you, and you will live. I will place you upon your land, and you will know that I, the Lord, have spoken and will act, says the Lord.’

target_units.text: And if the Spirit of the One who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, the One who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit dwelling in you.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel use of inscribed tribal staffs as visible divine signs
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel writes Judah and Joseph-Ephraim on two staffs to depict joining. Numbers prescribes named staffs for ancestral houses, with Aaron's name on Levi's staff, for a sign of divine choosing; the signs and number of staffs differ.
retained_triples.source_text: ‘Son of man, take a staff for yourself and write upon it Judah and Israel’s sons attached to him. Take a second staff for yourself and write upon it, For Joseph—Ephraim’s staff—and all Israel’s sons joined to him.

target_units.text: Speak to the sons of Israel and take from them one staff for each ancestral house, from all their leaders according to their ancestral houses—twelve staffs. Write each man’s name on his staff.
And write Aaron’s name on Levi’s staff, for they shall give one staff for each tribe of their ancestral houses.
And you shall place them in the Tent of Testimony, opposite the testimony, where I will make Myself known unto you.
And the staff of the man I choose shall sprout. I will remove from Myself the sons of Israel’s grumbling, which they direct against you.

retained_triples.relationship: contrasting actions with staffs concerning Judah and Israel
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel binds staffs into one in the sign of reunion. Zechariah throws away the second staff to dissolve the possession between Judah and Israel; the source's joining contrasts with the target's throwing away without replacing its word possession.
retained_triples.source_text: Join them to one another for yourself as one staff, binding them together, and they will be in your hand.

target_units.text: I threw away the second staff, Measuring Cord, to dissolve the possession between Judah and Israel.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel request for interpretation of a prophetic sign
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel anticipates the people's request to explain the staffs. In the earlier acted sign the people likewise ask what his conduct means, and he interprets the mourning sign; the visible actions themselves differ.
retained_triples.source_text: When your people’s sons say to you, Will you not tell us what these things mean to you?

target_units.text: The people said to me, “Will you not tell us what these things are that you are doing?”
I said to them, “The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

‘Say to Israel’s house, Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am profaning My holy things, the boast of your strength, the desires of your eyes, those for whom your souls care. Your sons and daughters whom you left behind will fall by the sword.
You will do as I have done: you will not be comforted from their mouth or eat the bread of men,
with your hair upon your heads and your footwear on your feet. You certainly will neither beat your breasts nor weep; you will waste away in your injustices and each will comfort his brother.
Ezekiel will be a portent for you; according to everything he has done, you will do when these things come. You will recognize that I am the Lord.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel reunion of Judah and Israel under common authority
retained_triples.rationale: The staff's interpretation joins Joseph-Ephraim and attached tribes to Judah as one staff in Judah's hand. Hosea likewise joins Judah's and Israel's sons gathering and appointing one authority; it does not use Ezekiel's staff imagery.
retained_triples.source_text: say to them, Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will take Joseph’s tribe through Ephraim’s hand, and Israel’s tribes attached to him, and place them upon Judah’s tribe. They will become one staff in Judah’s hand.

target_units.text: Judah’s sons and Israel’s sons will gather together, appoint one authority for themselves and come up from the land, for great is Jezreel’s day.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel public presentation of the tribal staffs
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel must hold the inscribed staffs before the people. Numbers describes Moses bringing the tribal staffs before all Israel, who look at them; the earlier context concerns the sprouted staff, whereas Ezekiel's sign concerns joining.
retained_triples.source_text: The staffs upon which you wrote will be in your hand before them,

target_units.text: And Moses brought all the staffs out from before the Lord to all the sons of Israel. They looked, and each man took his staff.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel gathering from nations into Israel's land
retained_triples.rationale: Both promises gather the dispersed people from nations and return them to their inherited land. Ezekiel expressly names all Israel's house and Israel's land.
retained_triples.source_text: and say to them, Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am taking all Israel’s house from among the nations where they entered, gathering them from all those around them and bringing them into Israel’s land.

target_units.text: then the Lord shall heal your sins, and have mercy upon you, and shall gather you again from all the nations whither the Lord has scattered you.
If your dispersion is from one end of heaven unto the other end of heaven, from thence shall the Lord your God gather you, and from thence shall the Lord your God take you.
And the Lord your God shall bring you into the land which your fathers inherited, and you shall inherit it; and He shall do you good, and make you more numerous than your fathers.

retained_triples.relationship: close parallel reunion under a single ruler
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises one nation and ruler instead of two kingdoms. Hosea likewise promises Judah's and Israel's sons gathering together and appointing one authority.
retained_triples.source_text: I will make them one nation in My land and upon Israel’s mountains, and one ruler will be theirs. They will no longer be two nations or ever again be divided into two kingdoms,

target_units.text: Judah’s sons and Israel’s sons will gather together, appoint one authority for themselves and come up from the land, for great is Jezreel’s day.

retained_triples.relationship: repeated combination of cleansing from idols and covenant belonging
retained_triples.rationale: Both restoration promises cleanse the people from their defilement and idols and declare that they will be God's people and He their God. The preceding oracle additionally describes clean water and a renewed heart and spirit.
retained_triples.source_text: so that they no longer defile themselves with their idols. I will deliver them from all their lawless deeds in which they sinned and cleanse them. They will be My people, and I, the Lord, will be their God.

target_units.text: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you will be cleansed from all your uncleannesses and all your idols. I will cleanse you.
And I will give you a new heart, and I will give a new spirit within you; and I will take the heart of stone out of your flesh, and give you a heart of flesh.
I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My ordinances, keep My judgments and do them.
You will dwell upon the land I gave your fathers. You will be My people, and I will be your God.

retained_triples.relationship: close parallel one shepherd called God's servant David
retained_triples.rationale: Both passages appoint God's servant David over the people and speak of one shepherd. The source also connects this rule with the people's keeping God's ordinances and judgments.
retained_triples.source_text: My servant David will be ruler among them, and one shepherd will be over all, because they will walk in My ordinances, keep My judgments and do them.

target_units.text: I will raise up one shepherd over them, My servant David, and he will shepherd them and be their shepherd.
I, the Lord, will be their God, and David a ruler among them. I, the Lord, have spoken.

retained_triples.relationship: related promise of enduring Davidic rule
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel calls David God's servant and promises his rule for ever. The oracle to David in 2 Samuel promises an offspring whose house, kingdom and throne are established for ever; the passages describe the ruler differently, so the link does not settle an individual identification.
retained_triples.source_text: They will dwell upon their land, which I gave My servant Jacob, where their fathers dwelt. They will dwell upon it, and David My servant will be their ruler for ever.

target_units.text: When your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you, who will be from your own body, and prepare his kingdom.
He will build Me a house for My name, and I will set his throne upright for ever.
I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to Me. If his wrongdoing comes, I will correct him with the rod of men and the afflictions of human beings.
But I will not withdraw My mercy from him as I withdrew it from those whom I removed from before Me.
His house and his kingdom will be made sure for ever before Me, and his throne will be set upright for ever.’”

retained_triples.relationship: parallel enduring covenant of peace
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises an everlasting covenant of peace. Isaiah likewise declares that the covenant of peace will not be removed and grounds it in divine mercy; Ezekiel also places God's holy things among the people.
retained_triples.source_text: I will make a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting covenant with them. I will set My holy things among them for ever.

target_units.text: “This dates for Me from the water in Noah’s time, when I swore to him then concerning the earth not to be angry with you again, nor at a threat against you
for mountains to move away; nor will your hills be shifted. So neither will My mercy toward you fail, nor will your covenant of peace ever be removed.” For the Lord said, “I am gracious to you.”

retained_triples.relationship: close parallel dwelling and reciprocal God-and-people declaration
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel promises God's dwelling among the people and declares that He will be their God and they His people. Paul's temple exhortation repeats divine dwelling and the same reciprocal declaration, also mentioning God's walking among them.
retained_triples.source_text: My dwelling will be among them. I will be their God, and they will be My people.

target_units.text: And what agreement is there between God’s temple and idols? For we are the temple of the living God, just as God said: “I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.

retained_triples.relationship: related holy presence and recognition of Israel's God
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel joins God's sanctifying the people with His holy things among them and the nations' recognition. Exodus joins consecration of the Tent and priests with God's being called upon among Israel and the people's recognition of their God; its audience of recognition differs.
retained_triples.source_text: The nations will know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them, when My holy things are among them for ever.’

target_units.text: There I will appoint Myself for the sons of Israel, and I will be sanctified in My glory.
I will consecrate the Tent of Testimony and the altar. I will also consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests.
I will be called upon among the sons of Israel and be their God.
They shall know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt to be called upon among them and to be their God.”

retained_triples.relationship: repeated commission against Gog with the same associated names
retained_triples.rationale: Both directives tell Ezekiel to prophesy against Gog and name Rhos, Mosoch and Thobel in describing him. The source additionally names the land of Magog; the comparison does not assign any of these names a modern geographical identity.
retained_triples.source_text: “Son of man, set your face firmly against Gog and the land of Magog, ruler of Rhos, Mosoch and Thobel, and prophesy against him,

target_units.text: “And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Gog, ruler of Rhos, Mosoch and Thobel,

retained_triples.relationship: close repeated declaration of opposition to Gog
retained_triples.rationale: Both oracles declare that God is against Gog and repeat the same description involving Rhos, Mosoch and Thobel. This is a textual correspondence within the Gog oracles, without an external identification of the ruler.
retained_triples.source_text: and say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Gog, ruler of Rhos, Mosoch and Thobel,

target_units.text: “And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Gog, ruler of Rhos, Mosoch and Thobel,

retained_triples.relationship: parallel descriptions of equipped foreign cavalry and troops
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel lists horses, horsemen, breastplates, shields and helmets in Gog's force. Jeremiah's command to the Egyptian force likewise names horses, riders, helmets, breastplates and shields; its spears and Ezekiel's swords are not treated as identical equipment.
retained_triples.source_text: and I will gather you and all your force, horses and horsemen all clothed in breastplates, a great assembly, small shields, helmets and swords,

target_units.text: Take up weapons and shields, and advance to war!
Saddle the horses; mount, riders! Take your positions in your helmets. Hold your spears forward; put on your breastplates!

retained_triples.relationship: shared foreign contingents and defensive equipment
retained_triples.rationale: Gog's force includes Persians and Libyans with helmets and small shields. The Tyre oracle also names Persians and Libyans with small shields and helmets, but includes Lydians where the source names Ethiopians and serves a different force.
retained_triples.source_text: Persians, Ethiopians and Libyans, all with helmets and small shields;

target_units.text: Persians, Lydians, and Libyans were in your force; your warrior men hung small shields and helmets in you; they gave you your glory.

retained_triples.relationship: shared Ethiopian and Libyan warriors in different forces
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel includes Ethiopians and Libyans among Gog's equipped troops. Jeremiah's oracle concerning Pharaoh's force likewise calls out Ethiopian and Libyan warriors with weapons; neither passage makes these two armies the same event.
retained_triples.source_text: Persians, Ethiopians and Libyans, all with helmets and small shields;

target_units.text: Mount the horses; prepare the chariots! Go out, warriors of the Ethiopians and Libyans equipped with weapons! And Lydians, go up and draw the bow!

retained_triples.relationship: earlier restoration promise reflected in the land awaiting invasion
retained_triples.rationale: The source describes people gathered from nations to formerly desolate Israel and dwelling in peace. The earlier promise gathers Israel from nations into its given land and describes settling there in hope, building houses and planting vineyards.
retained_triples.source_text: After many days he will be prepared, and at the end of years he will come and reach the land turned back from the sword, of those gathered from many nations, upon Israel’s land that had been wholly desolate. This one has come out of nations, and all will dwell in peace.

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will gather Israel from the nations where they were scattered, and I will be sanctified in them before the peoples and the nations. They will dwell on their land, which I have given to My servant Jacob,

and they will dwell on it in hope, build houses, and plant vineyards. They will dwell in hope when I execute judgment on all around them who dishonored them. They will know that I am the Lord their God and the God of their fathers.”

retained_triples.relationship: close weather imagery for an advancing enemy force
retained_triples.rationale: Gog's assembly comes like rain and a cloud covering the land. Jeremiah depicts an advancing enemy like a cloud and his chariots like a storm; the cloud image corresponds without identifying Jeremiah's enemy as Gog.
retained_triples.source_text: You will come up like rain and arrive like a cloud to cover the land; you will be there, with all those around you and many nations with you.

target_units.text: Behold, he will come up like a cloud, and his chariots like a storm; his horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, because we suffer misery!

retained_triples.relationship: parallel evil planning directed toward plunder
retained_triples.rationale: Gog devises evil plans, specified in the following units as attacking and plundering settled people. Micah condemns people who plan evil on their beds and then covet fields and plunder people, houses and inheritances; the scale and actors differ.
retained_triples.source_text: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: On that day words will rise in your heart, and you will devise evil plans,

target_units.text: They became people planning troubles and working evil on their beds, and at daybreak they carried them out, because they did not raise their hands to God.
They coveted fields and plundered orphans, oppressed houses and plundered a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.

retained_triples.relationship: related aggressive designs on a quietly settled people
retained_triples.rationale: Gog proposes to attack those resting quietly and living in peace. The Danite scouts similarly describe Laish's people living in confidence and urge an attack; Judges does not supply Ezekiel's explicit absence of walls, bars and doors.
retained_triples.source_text: and say, “I will go up against an abandoned land; I will come upon those resting quietly and dwelling in peace, all living in a land with no wall or bars, and they have no doors,”

target_units.text: The five men went and came to Laish. They saw the people dwelling there living in confidence, after the Sidonians’ pattern, resting in confidence and unable to speak a word, because they were far from Sidon and had no dealings with Syria.
The five men came to their brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol. Their brothers said to them, “Why are you sitting here?”

They said, “Arise, and let us go up against them; for we entered and walked through the land as far as Laish, and saw the people dwelling there in confidence, after the manner of the Sidonians, far from Sidon and without dealings with Syria. But arise, let us go up against them; for we have found the land, and behold, it is very good. Do you remain silent? Do not delay to go in and inherit the land.
When you enter, you shall come to a people dwelling in confidence, and the land is spacious. God has delivered it into your hands, a place lacking nothing that is upon the earth.”

retained_triples.relationship: restored desolate land becomes the object of the invader's plunder
retained_triples.rationale: Gog aims at a formerly desolate land now inhabited and a people accumulating possessions. The earlier promise describes precisely such a transition from devastated places to inhabited cities and worked land; it does not explain the source's earth's-navel phrase.
retained_triples.source_text: to take plunder and strip their spoils, to turn your hand against the desolate land that was inhabited and against a nation gathered from many nations, acquiring possessions, dwelling upon the earth’s navel.

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord: On the day I cleanse you from all your lawless deeds, I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the wilderness places will be rebuilt.
The devastated land will be worked, instead of lying devastated before every passerby’s eyes.
They will say, “That devastated land has become like a garden of delight, and the deserted, devastated, razed cities stand fortified.”

retained_triples.relationship: shared Carthaginian merchants associated with silver and gold
retained_triples.rationale: The source names Carthaginian merchants among those asking whether Gog seeks silver and gold as plunder. The Tyre trading list also names Carthaginians and their silver and gold, in commerce rather than the source's inquiry about spoils.
retained_triples.source_text: Saba, Daidan, Carthaginian merchants and all their villages will say to you, “Are you coming for plunder, to plunder and strip spoils? Have you gathered your assembly to take silver and gold, carry away possessions and strip spoils?”

target_units.text: Carthaginians were your traders because of the abundance of all your strength; they gave silver, gold, iron, tin, and lead for your market.

retained_triples.relationship: related stirring of an aggressor against a confident population
retained_triples.rationale: The question asks whether Gog will be roused when Israel is settled in peace. The scouts urge their brothers to arise and invade a land whose people dwell in confidence; the comparison concerns aggressive response to security, not the identity of the peoples.
retained_triples.source_text: Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog, Thus says the Lord: On that day when My people Israel are settled in peace, will you not be roused?

target_units.text: They said, “Arise, and let us go up against them; for we entered and walked through the land as far as Laish, and saw the people dwelling there in confidence, after the manner of the Sidonians, far from Sidon and without dealings with Syria. But arise, let us go up against them; for we have found the land, and behold, it is very good. Do you remain silent? Do not delay to go in and inherit the land.
When you enter, you shall come to a people dwelling in confidence, and the land is spacious. God has delivered it into your hands, a place lacking nothing that is upon the earth.”

retained_triples.relationship: close repeated northern approach of Gog
retained_triples.rationale: The source brings Gog and many nations from the farthest north. The following oracle likewise says God will bring him from the farthest north onto Israel's mountains; it does not repeat the cavalry inventory.
retained_triples.source_text: You will come from your place in the farthest north, with many nations beside you, all horse riders, a great assembly and a mighty force,

target_units.text: and I will gather you, lead you along, bring you up from the farthest north and bring you upon Israel’s mountains.

retained_triples.relationship: shared public sanctification before the nations in different settings
retained_triples.rationale: God brings Gog against His land so nations know Him when He is sanctified before them. The restoration oracle likewise promises public sanctification and the nations' knowledge, but there the immediate setting is His action in Israel rather than the invading Gog.
retained_triples.source_text: and come up against My people Israel like a cloud covering the land. It will be at the end of days; I will bring you against My land so that all the nations may know Me when I am sanctified in you before them.

target_units.text: I will sanctify My great name, profaned among the nations, which you profaned among them. The nations will know that I am the Lord when I am sanctified in you before their eyes.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel day announcements within the Gog oracles
retained_triples.rationale: The source announces the day Gog comes and God's wrath rises. The following Gog oracle declares arrival and future knowledge, calling this the day on which God spoke. The link concerns their related day declarations, without changing on which to of which or claiming an observed historical fulfillment.
retained_triples.source_text: On that day, on the day Gog comes against Israel’s land, says the Lord, the Lord, My wrath will rise,

target_units.text: Behold, it has arrived, and you will know that it will be, says the Lord, the Lord. This is the day on which I spoke.

retained_triples.relationship: parallel shaking of the land before divine anger
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel connects jealousy and fiery anger with a great shaking of Israel's land. Nahum likewise places shaking mountains and earth beside God's furious wrath and crushed rocks; its geographical scope differs.
retained_triples.source_text: and My jealousy. In the fire of My anger I have spoken: Surely on that day there will be a great shaking upon Israel’s land,

target_units.text: Mountains shook before Him and hills were shaken; the whole earth recoiled before Him, and all who dwell in it.
Who will stand before His anger? Who will resist His furious wrath? His fury melts rulers, and rocks were crushed before Him.

retained_triples.relationship: close terrestrial convulsion before the Lord
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel describes creatures and humans shaking, with mountains splitting and ravines and walls falling. Nahum similarly describes mountains and hills shaking, the earth recoiling and rocks crushed before God's anger, without Ezekiel's full creature catalogue.
retained_triples.source_text: and the sea’s fish, the sky’s birds, the plain’s beasts, every creeping thing upon the earth and every human upon the earth’s face will shake before the Lord. The mountains will split, the ravines will fall, and every wall will fall to the ground.

target_units.text: Mountains shook before Him and hills were shaken; the whole earth recoiled before Him, and all who dwell in it.
Who will stand before His anger? Who will resist His furious wrath? His fury melts rulers, and rocks were crushed before Him.

retained_triples.relationship: related comprehensive shaking involving earth and nations
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel's shaking reaches sea creatures, birds, earthly creatures and every human, with collapsing terrain. Haggai promises shaking of heaven, earth, sea, dry land and all nations; its setting concerns the house's coming glory rather than Gog's attack.
retained_triples.source_text: and the sea’s fish, the sky’s birds, the plain’s beasts, every creeping thing upon the earth and every human upon the earth’s face will shake before the Lord. The mountains will split, the ravines will fall, and every wall will fall to the ground.

target_units.text: For thus says the Lord Almighty: Once more I will shake heaven and earth, the sea and the dry land.
And I will shake all the nations, and the choice things of all the nations shall come; and I will fill this house with glory, says the Lord Almighty.

retained_triples.relationship: close judgment through swords turned against companions
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel announces that a man's sword will be against his brother. In Gideon's battle the Lord sets each man's sword against his neighbor throughout the enemy camp; the target supplies a narrated instance of this form of defeat.
retained_triples.source_text: I will summon every fear against him, says the Lord. A man’s sword will be against his brother.

target_units.text: The three hundred horn trumpets sounded, and the Lord set each man’s sword against his neighbour throughout the camp. The camp fled as far as Beth-shittah and, gathered together, as far as the edge of Abel-meholah and toward Tabbath.

retained_triples.relationship: close divine rain of fire and sulfur
retained_triples.rationale: God threatens to rain fire and sulfur on Gog and his accompanying nations. Genesis records the Lord raining sulfur and fire upon Sodom and Gomorrah; the judged peoples and settings differ.
retained_triples.source_text: I will judge him with death, blood, flooding rain and hailstones. I will rain fire and sulfur upon him, all those with him and the many nations with him.

target_units.text: And the Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah sulphur and fire from the Lord out of the heaven;

retained_triples.relationship: related destruction of an enemy force by divinely sent hailstones
retained_triples.rationale: Ezekiel includes hailstones among judgments against Gog's force. Joshua records the Lord hurling hailstones from heaven on a fleeing enemy force, causing more deaths than Israel's sword; Ezekiel supplies no such numerical comparison.
retained_triples.source_text: I will judge him with death, blood, flooding rain and hailstones. I will rain fire and sulfur upon him, all those with him and the many nations with him.

target_units.text: As they fled before the sons of Israel down the descent of Horonin, the Lord hurled hailstones from heaven upon them as far as Azekah. More died from the hailstones than the sons of Israel killed with the sword in battle.

retained_triples.relationship: related divine judgment combining hail and fire
